summary: Static review of start-prod.bat already-running detection + start-dev.bat message; sanity check of /api/health. No concrete bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: (a) OK: goto :ready inside parenthesized if-block is valid; it abandons the block and jumps to :ready (line 47) in the same file.
(b) OK: 'if not errorlevel 1' is evaluated at runtime (not %errorlevel% expansion), so it correctly reflects findstr's exit code from the pipeline (findstr is the last command).

(c) OK: curl.exe ships in System32 on Win10 1803+/11; _env.bat prepends System32 to PATH. '2>nul' before the pipe is valid and only applies to curl. On older Windows without curl, findstr fails and the script falls back to the 'another program' message - safe degradation.
(d) OK: no ( or ) in echo text inside the block (lines 25-31).
(e) OK: CRLF on all lines in start-prod.bat (67/67), start-dev.bat (50/50), _env.bat (24/24).
(f) OK: :ready section is self-contained (LANIP reset, ipconfig loop, start browser, exit /b 0); works when reached early.
Optional hardening (not a bug): use 'curl -s -m 3 --noproxy * http://127.0.0.1:%BACKEND_PORT%/api/health' to avoid a system HTTP_PROXY env var or ::1 resolution interfering.
start-dev.bat line 21 message fine; no parens, CRLF intact.
context_for_next_testing_agent: GET http://localhost:8001/api/health returns {"status":"healthy","service":"machinery-erp"} - matches findstr string. Batch files reviewed statically only (no cmd.exe).
